recall_prompt: Say how you would find the mean deviation about the mean for eight numbers — what you find first and what you average at the end.
insider_note: The mean is exactly 10, so the value 10 contributes a zero deviation — it still counts in n = 8; dividing the sum 26 by 7 instead of 8 loses the second mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mean
steps.margin_note: First mark. Eight values, sum 80, mean 10. Write n = 8 — it is the divisor in both steps.
steps.memory_tip: 80/8 = 10. The repeated 12 is counted twice, so n = 8 and the same 8 divides the next step.

recall.must_convey: That the mean of the eight values is 80/8 = 10.
accept: add the eight numbers to get eighty and divide by eight, the mean is ten
x bar is eighty by eight equals ten
the mean of the data is ten
enimidi numbers add cheste eighty, eight tho divide cheste mean ten
sum eighty, n eight, mean ten

steps.why: Mean deviation is measured from the mean, so the mean has to exist first. The signed deviations from the mean add to zero, which is why the next step drops the signs.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 7 because 12 appears twice — n counts every value, so n = 8.

steps.label: Mean deviation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the eight absolute deviations from 10, add them (26), divide by n = 8. 26/8 = 3.25 exactly.
steps.memory_tip: The value 10 equals the mean, so its deviation is 0 — but it still counts in n = 8. 26/8 = 3.25.

recall.must_convey: That the absolute deviations from 10 are 4, 3, 0, 2, 3, 6, 2, 6, their sum 26 divided by 8 gives 3.25.
accept: take each number minus ten without sign, add to twenty six, divide by eight, three point two five
the absolute deviations add to twenty six and twenty six by eight is three point two five
mean deviation is sigma mod x i minus x bar by n equals twenty six by eight equals three point two five
ten nunchi deviations mod teesukoni add cheste twenty six, eight tho divide cheste three point two five
the answer is three point two five

steps.why: Mean deviation is the average distance from the mean. The absolute value is what stops the distances cancelling — without it the total is 0 for every data set.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the value 10 itself, which contributes 0 but still counts in n = 8.
